title: Think about the thing you protect
summary: An asset is something valuable, such as a file or saved work. A threat is something that might harm it. A risk considers how likely and harmful that problem is.
introduction: An asset is something valuable, such as a file or saved work. A threat is something that might harm it. A risk considers how likely and harmful that problem is. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain think about the thing you protect
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An asset is something valuable, such as a file or saved work. A threat is something that might harm it. A risk considers how likely and harmful that problem is.

blocks.code:
Asset: a class project file
Threat: accidental deletion
Control: a tested backup copy
blocks.title: Think about the thing you protect

blocks.text: The backup reduces the harm from losing the working file.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name a threat to a shared classroom tablet and one useful protection.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not start with a tool before naming the problem it should reduce.
For more detail later, use this [Cybersecurity Fundamentals further reading](https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world).
